# Lab 18.6: Dynamic Data Masking

## What We Are Going to Do
Instead of blocking the PII column, show masked values (hashed, nulled, default or custom) depending on who asks.

## Steps

1. **[Console] Create a masking rule.** In **Governance → Security centre → Policy management** (or the taxonomy page), open the **PII** policy tag → **Manage data policies → Add rule**:
   - **Masking rule**: Hash (SHA-256)
   - **Principal**: the `bq-analyst` service account (as **Masked Reader**)

2. **[CLI] Check the data policy.**

curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \

3. **[CLI] Query as the analyst.**

bq query --use_legacy_sql=false 'SELECT first_name, email FROM lab18_private.users LIMIT 5'
gcloud config unset auth/impersonate_service_account</span>
</code></pre>

   The analyst sees a hash instead of the email. Hashes stay the same for the same value, so joins and counts still work.

4. **[SQL] Create a custom masking routine.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION lab18_private.mask_email(email STRING)
RETURNS STRING
OPTIONS (data_governance_type = 'DATA_MASKING')
AS (CONCAT(LEFT(email, 2), '****@', SPLIT(email, '@')[SAFE_OFFSET(1)]));</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Change the masking rule to **Custom masking routine → mask_email**. The analyst now sees `as****@example.com`.

5. **[Console] Try Nullify and Default value.** Switch the rule and query again to compare.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Fine-Grained Reader | Real values |
| Masked Reader | Masked values |
| Others | Access denied |
| Custom routine | Your own masking logic |
